PART XVIII
EMERGENCY PROVISIONS 
352. Proclamation of Emergency.—(1) If the President is satisfied that 
a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the 
territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or 1[armed 
rebellion], he may, by Proclamation, make a declaration to that effect 2[in 
respect of the whole of India or of such part of the territory thereof as may be 
specified in the Proclamation.] 
3[Explanation.—A Proclamation of Emergency declaring that the 
security of India or any part of the territory thereof is threatened by war or by 
external aggression or by armed rebellion may be made before the actual 
occurrence of war or of any such aggression or rebellion, if the President is 
satisfied that there is imminent danger thereof.] 
4[(2) A Proclamation issued under clause (1) may be varied or revoked 
by a subsequent Proclamation.
(3) The President shall not issue a Proclamation under clause (1) or a 
Proclamation varying such Proclamation unless the decision of the Union 
Cabinet (that is to say, the Council consisting of the Prime Minister and other 
Ministers of Cabinet rank appointed under article 75) that such a Proclamation 
may be issued has been communicated to him in writing.
(4) Every Proclamation issued under this article shall be laid before each 
House of Parliament and shall, except where it is a Proclamation revoking a 
previous Proclamation, cease to operate at the expiration of one month unless 
before the expiration of that period it has been approved by resolutions of both 
Houses of Parliament:

nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the emergency provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the procedures and powers associated with the declaration of a state of emergency. Key points include:

1. **Resolution for Disapproval**: A mechanism for the House of the People to disapprove a Proclamation of Emergency, requiring a notice signed by at least one-tenth of its members, and the necessity for a special sitting within fourteen days to consider such a resolution.

2. **Presidential Powers**: The President has the authority to issue multiple Proclamations based on different grounds such as war, external aggression, or armed rebellion, even if a Proclamation is already in effect.

3. **Effect of Emergency**: During an emergency, the Union's executive power can direct states on how to exercise their executive powers, and Parliament can legislate on matters not listed in the Union List if necessary for the emergency.

4. **Revenue Distribution**: The President can modify the application of revenue distribution provisions during an emergency, with any orders needing to be presented to Parliament.

5. **Union's Duty**: The Union is responsible for protecting states against external aggression and internal disturbances, ensuring that state governments operate according to the Constitution.

6. **Failure of Constitutional Machinery**: The President can proclaim a state of emergency if it is determined that a state's government cannot function according to constitutional provisions, based on reports from the Governor or other sources.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the provisions regarding the official language of the Union as stated in Chapter I of Part XVII. It establishes Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language, while allowing the continued use of English for official purposes for a period of fifteen years from the Constitution's commencement. The document also mentions that the President can authorize the use of Hindi and Devanagari numerals during this period. Additionally, it discusses the establishment of a Commission by the President after five and ten years to recommend the progressive use of Hindi, potential restrictions on English, and the language for specific official purposes.

PART XVII
OFFICIAL LANGUAGE
CHAPTER I.—LANGUAGE OF THE UNION
343. Official language of the Union.—(1) The official language of the 
Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union 
shall be the international form of Indian numerals.
(2) Notwithstanding anything in clause (1), for a period of fifteen years 
from the commencement of this Constitution, the English language shall 
continue to be used for all the official purposes of the Union for which it was 
being used immediately before such commencement: 
Provided that the President may, during the said period, by order1
authorise the use of the Hindi language in addition to the English language and 
of the Devanagari form of numerals in addition to the international form of 
Indian numerals for any of the official purposes of the Union.
(3) Notwithstanding anything in this article, Parliament may by law 
provide for the use, after the said period of fifteen years, of—
(a) the English language; or
(b) the Devanagari form of numerals,
for such purposes as may be specified in the law.
344. Commission and Committee of Parliament on official 
language.—(1) The President shall, at the expiration of five years from the 
commencement of this Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of ten years 
from such commencement, by order constitute a Commission which shall 
consist of a Chairman and such other members representing the different 
languages specified in the Eighth Schedule as the President may appoint, and 
the order shall define the procedure to be followed by the Commission.
(2) It shall be the duty of the Commission to make recommendations to 
the President as to—
(a) the progressive use of the Hindi language for the official 
purposes of the Union;
(b) restrictions on the use of the English language for all or any of 
the official purposes of the Union;
(c) the language to be used for all or any of the purposes 
mentioned in article 348;
______________________________________________
1. See C.O. 41.

nodes.title: Exercise of legislative powers under Proclamation issued under article 356.
nodes.summary: The partial document discusses the emergency provisions outlined in Part XVIII of the Constitution of India. It details the conditions under which a Proclamation of Emergency can be extended beyond one year, requiring both the existence of an emergency and certification from the Election Commission regarding the necessity of the extension. It also outlines the legislative powers that can be exercised by Parliament or the President during such emergencies, including the ability to make laws and authorize expenditures. Additionally, it addresses the suspension of certain rights under Article 19 during emergencies, allowing the state to take necessary actions for security, while stipulating that such laws will cease to have effect once the emergency is lifted. The document includes references to amendments that have modified these provisions over time.

nodes.title: Suspension of provisions of article 19 during emergencies.
nodes.summary: The partial document discusses the emergency provisions outlined in Part XVIII of the Constitution of India. It covers the legislative powers during a state of emergency, specifically under Article 356 and Article 358, which allow the Parliament or the President to enact laws that would not normally be within their competence due to the emergency declaration. It also addresses the suspension of certain rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution during emergencies, particularly the right to move courts for enforcement of these rights, as specified in Article 359. The document highlights the conditions under which these provisions apply, including the requirement for laws to explicitly relate to the emergency proclamation and the limitations on executive actions taken during this period. Additionally, it notes that certain rights, specifically Articles 20 and 21, remain unaffected by these emergency provisions.

nodes.title: Suspension of the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III during emergencies.
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the emergency provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the suspension of rights during a Proclamation of Emergency. It details the President's authority to suspend the enforcement of certain rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution, excluding articles 20 and 21, and the conditions under which such suspensions can occur. The document also discusses the limitations on laws and executive actions taken during an emergency, emphasizing that any such actions must include a specific recital relating to the emergency. Additionally, it addresses the process for declaring a financial emergency, including the President's ability to issue a proclamation if the financial stability of India is threatened, and the requirement for such proclamations to be presented to Parliament.

It details the limitations on laws and executive actions during an emergency, the scope of orders issued under such a proclamation, and the requirement for parliamentary approval of these proclamations. MISCELLANEOUS
361. Protection of President and Governors and Rajpramukhs.—(1) 
The President, or the Governor or Rajpramukh of a State, shall not be 
answerable to any court for the exercise and performance of the powers and 
duties of his office or for any act done or purporting to be done by him in the 
exercise and performance of those powers and duties: 
Provided that the conduct of the President may be brought under review 
by any court, tribunal or body appointed or designated by either House of 
Parliament for the investigation of a charge under article 61:
Provided further that nothing in this clause shall be construed as 
restricting the right of any person to bring appropriate proceedings against the 
Government of India or the Government of a State.
(2) No criminal proceedings whatsoever shall be instituted or continued 
against the President, or the Governor 1*** of a State, in any court during his 
term of office.
(3) No process for the arrest or imprisonment of the President, or the 
Governor 1*** of a State, shall issue from any court during his term of office.
(4) No civil proceedings in which relief is claimed against the President, 
or the Governor 1*** of a State, shall be instituted during his term of office in 
any court in respect of any act done or purporting to be done by him in his 
personal capacity, whether before or after he entered upon his office as 
President, or as Governor 1*** of such State, until the expiration of two months 
next after notice in writing has been delivered to the President or the Governor
1***, as the case may be, or left at his office stating the nature of the 
proceedings, the cause of action therefor, the name, description and place of 
residence of the party by whom such proceedings are to be instituted and the

The partial document discusses various provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically under Part XIX, which covers miscellaneous topics. Key points include:

1. **Government Employment and Remuneration**: It addresses the conditions under which individuals can hold office in bodies owned by the government and the nature of remuneration they receive.

2. **Rights and Privileges of Rulers**: It notes the omission of certain rights and privileges of rulers of Indian states following the Twenty-sixth Amendment in 1971, which abolished the recognition of these rulers and their privy purses.

3. **Judicial Jurisdiction**: Article 363 outlines the limitations on the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts regarding disputes arising from treaties or agreements made by rulers of Indian states before the Constitution came into effect.

4. **Special Provisions for Major Ports and Aerodromes**: Article 364 allows the President to issue notifications that can exempt major ports and aerodromes from certain laws or modify their application.

5. **State Compliance with Union Directives**: Article 365 states that if a state fails to comply with directives from the Union, the President can determine that the state government cannot function according to the Constitution.

6. **Definitions**: Article 366 provides definitions for specific terms used within the Constitution, such as "agricultural income" in relation to income tax laws.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the emergency provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the powers of the President during a state of emergency. It details the President's authority to assume functions of the state government, declare legislative powers to be exercised by Parliament, and make necessary provisions to implement the Proclamation. It also specifies limitations on the President's powers, particularly regarding High Courts. Additionally, the document describes the process for revoking or varying a Proclamation, the requirement for parliamentary approval within two months, and the conditions under which a Proclamation may cease to operate.

It outlines the requirements for ratification of amendments by state legislatures, clarifies that certain articles do not apply to these amendments, and asserts that amendments cannot be challenged in court. Additionally, it emphasizes the unlimited power of Parliament to amend the Constitution. The document also introduces Part XXI, which grants Parliament temporary powers to legislate on certain matters typically reserved for states, specifically for a period of five years from the Constitution's commencement. It details the scope of these powers and the conditions under which they will cease to be effective.

369. Temporary power to Parliament to make laws with respect to 
certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent 
List.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament shall, during 
a period of five years from the commencement of this Constitution, have power 
to make laws with respect to the following matters as if they were enumerated 
in the Concurrent List, namely:— 
(a) trade and commerce within a State in, and the production, supply 
and distribution of, cotton and woollen textiles, raw cotton (including 
ginned cotton and unginned cotton or kapas), cotton seed, paper 
(including newsprint), food-stuffs (including edible oilseeds and oil), 
cattle fodder (including oil-cakes and other concentrates), coal 
(including coke and derivatives of coal), iron, steel and mica;
(b) offences against laws with respect to any of the matters mentioned
in clause (a), jurisdiction and powers of all courts except the Supreme 
Court with respect to any of those matters, and fees in respect of any of 
those matters but not including fees taken in any court,
but any law made by Parliament, which Parliament would not but for the 
provisions of this article have been competent to make, shall, to the extent of the 
incompetency, cease to have effect on the expiration of the said period, except as 
respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration thereof.

nodes.title: Temporary, transitional and special provisions.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines various temporary, transitional, and special provisions in the Constitution of India, particularly focusing on the powers of Parliament and the President regarding specific states. Key points include:

1. **Temporary Powers of Parliament**: For five years from the Constitution's commencement, Parliament can legislate on certain matters in the State List as if they were in the Concurrent List, including trade, commerce, and production of specific goods.

2. **Provisions for Jammu and Kashmir**: Article 370 details the limited powers of Parliament to legislate for Jammu and Kashmir, emphasizing the need for consultation with the state government and the special status of the region.

3. **Special Provisions for Various States**: The document includes provisions for states like Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka, allowing for unique governance structures, legislative assemblies, and responsibilities of governors to address local needs and customs.

4. **Continuance of Existing Laws**: It states that existing laws will remain in force until amended or repealed, with the President having the authority to adapt these laws to align with the new Constitution within a specified timeframe.

Overall, the document emphasizes the flexibility and adaptability of the Constitution to accommodate the diverse needs of different states in India.

372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.—(1) 
Notwithstanding the repeal by this Constitution of the enactments referred to in 
article 395 but subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, all the law in 
force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended 
by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
(2) For the purpose of bringing the provisions of any law in force in the 
territory of India into accord with the provisions of this Constitution, the 
President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, 
whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and 
provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, 
have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(3) Nothing in clause (2) shall be deemed—
(a) to empower the President to make any adaptation or 
modification of any law after the expiration of 1[three years] from the 
commencement of this Constitution; or
(b) to prevent any competent Legislature or other competent 
authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by 
the President under the said clause.

(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)

(b) identification of posts or classes of posts under the State 
Government and in any body or organisation under the control of the 
State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region and reservation of

372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.—(1) 
Notwithstanding the repeal by this Constitution of the enactments referred to in 
article 395 but subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, all the law in 
force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended 
by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
(2) For the purpose of bringing the provisions of any law in force in the 
territory of India into accord with the provisions of this Constitution, the 
President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, 
whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and 
provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, 
have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(3) Nothing in clause (2) shall be deemed—
(a) to empower the President to make any adaptation or 
modification of any law after the expiration of 1[three years] from the 
commencement of this Constitution; or
(b) to prevent any competent Legislature or other competent 
authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by 
the President under the said clause.

Explanation I.—The expression “law in force” in this article shall 
include a law passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in 
the territory of India before the commencement of this Constitution and not 
previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in 
operation either at all or in particular areas.
Explanation II.—Any law passed or made by a Legislature or other 
competent authority in the territory of India which immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution had extra-territorial effect as well as effect 
in the territory of India shall, subject to any such adaptations and modifications 
as aforesaid, continue to have such extra-territorial effect.
Explanation III.—Nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing 
any temporary law in force beyond the date fixed for its expiration or the date 
on which it would have expired if this Constitution had  not come into force.
Explanation IV.—An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a 
Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and in force 
immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless 
withdrawn by the Governor of the corresponding State earlier, cease to operate 
at the expiration of six weeks from the first meeting after such commencement 
of the Legislative Assembly of that State functioning under clause (1) of article 
382, and  nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing any such 
Ordinance in force beyond the said period.

adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
248
373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines specific temporary, transitional, and special provisions of the Constitution of India, particularly focusing on the powers and roles of various judicial and governmental authorities following the Constitution's commencement. Key points include:

1. **Presidential Powers**: The President is granted the authority to make orders regarding preventive detention until Parliament enacts relevant provisions.

2. **Judges of the Federal Court**: Judges of the Federal Court automatically become Judges of the Supreme Court, with their existing rights and salaries preserved. Ongoing legal proceedings in the Federal Court are transferred to the Supreme Court.

3. **Jurisdiction of His Majesty in Council**: The document clarifies that the jurisdiction of His Majesty in Council remains valid for certain appeals and petitions, with orders made post-commencement treated as Supreme Court orders.

4. **Continuation of Courts and Authorities**: All existing courts, authorities, and officers will continue to function under the new Constitution's provisions.

5. **Judges of High Courts**: Judges of High Courts prior to the Constitution's commencement will transition to corresponding High Courts, retaining their rights and salaries, with specific provisions for judges from Indian States.

6. **Comptroller and Auditor-General**: The existing Auditor-General will become the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, maintaining their rights and term of office as per previous provisions.

Overall, the document emphasizes the continuity of judicial roles and the transition of powers and responsibilities as India adopts its new Constitution.

(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
249
375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and 
pension as are provided for under clause (3) of article 148 in respect of the 
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and be entitled to continue to hold office 
until the expiration of his term of office as determined under the provisions which 
were applicable to him immediately before such commencement.

The partial document outlines specific provisions of the Constitution of India related to the continuity of various judicial and administrative functions following its commencement. Key points include:

1. **Continuation of Courts and Authorities**: All courts and authorities in India will continue to operate under the new Constitution.
2. **Judges of High Courts**: Judges holding office before the Constitution's commencement will automatically become judges of the corresponding High Courts in the new states, with rights to salaries, allowances, and pensions as per the Constitution.
3. **Comptroller and Auditor-General**: The existing Auditor-General will transition to the role of Comptroller and Auditor-General under the new Constitution, retaining their rights and term of office.
4. **Public Service Commissions**: Members of existing Public Service Commissions will continue in their roles under the new framework unless they choose otherwise.
5. **Special Provisions for Andhra Pradesh**: The Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh is given a specific duration of five years, with provisions for its dissolution.
6. **Omissions**: Several provisions related to provisional Parliament, the President, and Governors have been omitted by subsequent amendments.

Overall, the document emphasizes the transition and continuity of governance structures in India as established by the new Constitution.

393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of

the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and

this Constitution made in the English language.

published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such

published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]

Furthermore, it begins the First Schedule, which lists the states and their territories, indicating the legal framework for the organization of states within India.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
248
373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
249
375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and 
pension as are provided for under clause (3) of article 148 in respect of the 
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and be entitled to continue to hold office 
until the expiration of his term of office as determined under the provisions which 
were applicable to him immediately before such commencement.

378. Provisions as to Public Service Commissions.—(1) The members 
of the Public Service Commission for the Dominion of India holding office 
immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they 
have elected otherwise, become on such commencement the members of the 
Public Service Commission for the Union and shall, notwithstanding anything in 
clauses (1) and (2) of article 316 but subject to the proviso to clause (2) of that 
article, continue to hold office until the expiration of their term of office as 
determined under the rules which were applicable immediately before such 
commencement to such members.
(2) The Members of a Public Service Commission of a Province or of a 
Public Service Commission serving the needs of a group of Provinces holding 
office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they 
have elected otherwise, become on such commencement the members of the Public

nodes.title: [Provision as to President.]
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines various temporary, transitional, and special provisions of the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the powers and roles of the President, judges, and public service commissions during the transition from the Government of India Act, 1935, to the new Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Preventive Detention**: The President has the authority to make orders regarding preventive detention until Parliament enacts provisions under Article 22.

2. **Judges of the Federal Court**: Judges from the Federal Court automatically become judges of the Supreme Court, with their previous judgments retaining validity.

3. **Judges of High Courts**: Existing High Court judges transition to corresponding High Courts in the new states, with provisions for their salaries and terms.

4. **Comptroller and Auditor-General**: The existing Auditor-General becomes the Comptroller and Auditor-General under the new Constitution.

5. **Public Service Commissions**: Members of existing Public Service Commissions transition to the new commissions, maintaining their terms.

6. **Special Provisions for Andhra Pradesh**: The Legislative Assembly of Andhra Pradesh is given a specific duration of five years unless dissolved earlier.

7. **Removal of Difficulties**: The President can issue orders to adapt the Constitution to remove difficulties during the transition period.

8. **Repeals**: The document also includes provisions for the repeal of previous acts, such as the Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the Government of India Act, 1935.

Overall, the document emphasizes the continuity of judicial and administrative functions while transitioning to the new constitutional framework.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
248
373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
249
375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and 
pension as are provided for under clause (3) of article 148 in respect of the 
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and be entitled to continue to hold office 
until the expiration of his term of office as determined under the provisions which 
were applicable to him immediately before such commencement.
______________________________________________
1. Added by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, s. 13 (w.e.f. 18-6-1951).

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
250
378. Provisions as to Public Service Commissions.—(1) The members 
of the Public Service Commission for the Dominion of India holding office 
immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they 
have elected otherwise, become on such commencement the members of the 
Public Service Commission for the Union and shall, notwithstanding anything in 
clauses (1) and (2) of article 316 but subject to the proviso to clause (2) of that 
article, continue to hold office until the expiration of their term of office as 
determined under the rules which were applicable immediately before such 
commencement to such members.
(2) The Members of a Public Service Commission of a Province or of a 
Public Service Commission serving the needs of a group of Provinces holding 
office immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they 
have elected otherwise, become on such commencement the members of the Public 
Service Commission for the corresponding State or the members of the Joint State 
Public Service Commission  serving the needs of the corresponding States, as the 
case may be, and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses (1) and (2) of article 
316 but subject to the proviso to clause (2) of that article, continue to hold office 
until the expiration of their term of office as determined under the rules which  were 
applicable immediately before such commencement to such members.
1[378A. Special provision as to duration of Andhra Pradesh 
Legislative Assembly.—Notwithstanding anything contained in article 172, the 
Legislative Assembly of the State of Andhra Pradesh as constituted under the 
provisions of sections 28 and 29 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, shall, 
unless sooner dissolved, continue for a period of five years from the date referred 
to in the said section 29 and no longer and the expiration of the said period shall 
operate as a dissolution of that Legislative Assembly.]

392. Power of the President to remove difficulties.—(1) The President 
may, for the purpose of removing any difficulties, particularly in relation to the 
transition from the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935, to the 
provisions of this Constitution, by order direct that this Constitution shall, 
during such period as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to such 
adaptations, whether by way of modification, addition or omission, as he may 
deem to be necessary or expedient:
Provided that no such order shall be made after the first meeting of 
Parliament duly constituted under Chapter II of Part V.
(2) Every order made under clause (1) shall be laid before Parliament.
(3) The powers conferred on the President by this article, by article 324, by 
clause (3) of article 367 and by article 391 shall, before the commencement of this 
Constitution, be exercisable by the Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

252
PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

It also outlines the continuance and adaptation of existing laws following the enactment of the Constitution of India. Specifically, it states that laws in force prior to the Constitution will remain effective until amended or repealed by competent authorities. The President is granted the authority to modify these laws to align them with the Constitution, with certain limitations on the duration and scope of this power. Additionally, it references various notifications related to the adaptation of laws.

State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region and reservation of 
a proportion of such posts for persons who belong to that region by birth 
or by domicile and for appointment thereto by direct recruitment or by 
promotion or in any other manner as may be specified in the order.]
372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.—(1) 
Notwithstanding the repeal by this Constitution of the enactments referred to in 
article 395 but subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, all the law in 
force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended 
by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
(2) For the purpose of bringing the provisions of any law in force in the 
territory of India into accord with the provisions of this Constitution, the 
President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, 
whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and 
provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, 
have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(3) Nothing in clause (2) shall be deemed—
(a) to empower the President to make any adaptation or 
modification of any law after the expiration of 1[three years] from the 
commencement of this Constitution; or
(b) to prevent any competent Legislature or other competent 
authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by 
the President under the said clause.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines provisions related to the salaries and entitlements of judges in the High Courts of India, as well as the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. It specifies that if a High Court judge is receiving a pension from previous government service, their salary will be reduced accordingly. It also details the rights of judges who transitioned from provincial courts to corresponding state High Courts upon the commencement of the Constitution, allowing them to receive special pay if their previous salary was higher. Additionally, it establishes the salary for the Comptroller and Auditor-General and ensures that their conditions of service, including leave and pension rights, are maintained as per previous regulations. The document also clarifies definitions related to judicial roles and service time.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Second Schedule) 
267
Provided that if a Judge of a High Court at the  time of his appointment is in 
receipt of a pension (other than a disability or wound pension) in respect of any 
previous service under the Government of India or any of its predecessor 
Governments or under  the Government of a State or any of its predecessor 
Governments, his salary in respect of service in the High Court shall be reduced—
(a) by the amount of that pension; and
(b) if he has, before such appointment, received in lieu of a portion of 
the pension due to him in respect of such previous service the commuted 
value thereof, by the amount of that portion of the pension; and
(c) if he has, before such appointment, received a retirement gratuity in 
respect of such previous service, by the pension equivalent of that 
gratuity.]
(2) Every person who immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution— 
(a) was holding office as the Chief Justice of a High Court in any 
Province and has on such commencement become the Chief Justice of the 
High Court in the corresponding State under clause (1) of article 376; or
(b) was holding office as any other Judge of a High Court in any Province 
and has on such commencement become a Judge (other than the Chief 
Justice) of the High Court in the corresponding State under the said clause,
shall, if he was immediately before such commencement drawing a salary at a 
rate higher than that specified in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph, be 
entitled to receive in respect of time spent on actual service as such Chief 
Justice or other Judge, as the case may be, in addition to the salary specified in 
the said sub-paragraph as special pay an amount equivalent to the difference 
between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing 
immediately before such commencement.
1[(3) Any person who, immediately before the commencement of the 
Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, was holding office as the Chief 
Justice of the High Court of  a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule 
and has on such commencement become the Chief Justice of the High Court of 
a State specified in the said Schedule as amended by the said Act, shall, if he 
was immediately before such commencement drawing any amount as 
allowance in addition to his salary, be entitled to receive in respect of time 
spent on actual service as such Chief Justice, the same amount as allowance in 
addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph.].
______________________________________________

sub-paragraphs (3) and (4) (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Second Schedule) 
268
11. In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) the expression “Chief Justice” includes an acting Chief Justice, 
and a “Judge” includes an ad hoc Judge; 
(b) “actual service” includes— 
(i) time spent by a Judge on duty as a Judge or in the performance 
of such other functions as he may at the request of the President 
undertake to discharge;
(ii) vacations, excluding any time during which the Judge is absent 
on leave; and
(iii) joining time on transfer from a High Court to the Supreme 
Court or from one High Court to another. 
PART E
PROVISIONS AS TO THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL OF INDIA 
12. (1) There shall be paid to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of 
India a salary at the rate of *four thousand rupees per mensem.
(2) The person who was holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution as Auditor-General of India and has 
become on such commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India 
under article 377 shall in addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1) of 
this paragraph be entitled to receive as special pay an amount equivalent to the 
difference between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing 
as Auditor-General of India immediately before such commencement.
(3) The rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and the other 
conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be 
governed or shall continue to be governed, as the case may be, by the provisions 
which were applicable to the Auditor-General of India immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution and all references in those provisions to the 
Governor-General shall be construed as references to the President.
______________________________________________
* The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be paid a salary equal to 
the salary of the Judges of the Supreme Court vide s. 3 of the Comptroller and 
Auditor-General (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 (56 of 
1971) .  The salary of Judges of the Supreme Court has been raised to two 
lakh fifty thousand rupees per mensem by the High Court and Supreme Court 
Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Act, 2018 (10 of 2018), s. 6 
(w.e.f. 1-1-2016).

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines key provisions of the Constitution of India, including its short title, commencement, and the authoritative text in Hindi. It specifies that the Constitution may be referred to as the Constitution of India and details the articles that came into force immediately versus those that took effect on January 26, 1950. Additionally, it mandates the publication of a Hindi translation of the Constitution and its amendments, establishing that this translation holds the same authoritative status as the original English text. The document also includes provisions for the repeal of previous acts, such as the Indian Independence Act of 1947 and the Government of India Act of 1935. Furthermore, it lists the First Schedule, which delineates the names and territories of various states and union territories in India, along with amendments and exclusions related to territorial boundaries. The Second Schedule addresses the emoluments and privileges of the President, Governors, and various legislative officials, while the Third Schedule provides forms of oaths for ministers and members of Parliament. Lastly, the Fourth Schedule allocates seats in the Council of States for each state and union territory.
nodes.text:
252
PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.
______________________________________________
1. Ins. by the Constitution (Fifty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1987, s. 2 (w.e.f. 9-12-1987).
2. Art 394A, Ins. by s. 3, ibid. (w.e.f. 9-12-1987).

provisions which, immediately before the commencement of this Constitution,  
were applicable to the Judges of the Federal Court.

(Second Schedule)

Provided that if a Judge of a High Court at the  time of his appointment is in 
receipt of a pension (other than a disability or wound pension) in respect of any 
previous service under the Government of India or any of its predecessor 
Governments or under  the Government of a State or any of its predecessor 
Governments, his salary in respect of service in the High Court shall be reduced—
(a) by the amount of that pension; and
(b) if he has, before such appointment, received in lieu of a portion of 
the pension due to him in respect of such previous service the commuted 
value thereof, by the amount of that portion of the pension; and
(c) if he has, before such appointment, received a retirement gratuity in 
respect of such previous service, by the pension equivalent of that 
gratuity.]
(2) Every person who immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution— 
(a) was holding office as the Chief Justice of a High Court in any 
Province and has on such commencement become the Chief Justice of the 
High Court in the corresponding State under clause (1) of article 376; or
(b) was holding office as any other Judge of a High Court in any Province 
and has on such commencement become a Judge (other than the Chief 
Justice) of the High Court in the corresponding State under the said clause,
shall, if he was immediately before such commencement drawing a salary at a 
rate higher than that specified in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph, be 
entitled to receive in respect of time spent on actual service as such Chief 
Justice or other Judge, as the case may be, in addition to the salary specified in 
the said sub-paragraph as special pay an amount equivalent to the difference 
between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing 
immediately before such commencement.
1[(3) Any person who, immediately before the commencement of the 
Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, was holding office as the Chief 
Justice of the High Court of  a State specified in Part B of the First Schedule 
and has on such commencement become the Chief Justice of the High Court of 
a State specified in the said Schedule as amended by the said Act, shall, if he 
was immediately before such commencement drawing any amount as 
allowance in addition to his salary, be entitled to receive in respect of time 
spent on actual service as such Chief Justice, the same amount as allowance in 
addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1) of this paragraph.].
______________________________________________

11. In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) the expression “Chief Justice” includes an acting Chief Justice, 
and a “Judge” includes an ad hoc Judge; 
(b) “actual service” includes— 
(i) time spent by a Judge on duty as a Judge or in the performance 
of such other functions as he may at the request of the President 
undertake to discharge;
(ii) vacations, excluding any time during which the Judge is absent 
on leave; and
(iii) joining time on transfer from a High Court to the Supreme 
Court or from one High Court to another. 
PART E
PROVISIONS AS TO THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL OF INDIA 
12. (1) There shall be paid to the Comptroller and Auditor-General of 
India a salary at the rate of *four thousand rupees per mensem.
(2) The person who was holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution as Auditor-General of India and has 
become on such commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India 
under article 377 shall in addition to the salary specified in sub-paragraph (1) of 
this paragraph be entitled to receive as special pay an amount equivalent to the 
difference between the salary so specified and the salary which he was drawing 
as Auditor-General of India immediately before such commencement.
(3) The rights in respect of leave of absence and pension and the other 
conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be 
governed or shall continue to be governed, as the case may be, by the provisions 
which were applicable to the Auditor-General of India immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution and all references in those provisions to the 
Governor-General shall be construed as references to the President.
______________________________________________
* The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India shall be paid a salary equal to 
the salary of the Judges of the Supreme Court vide s. 3 of the Comptroller and 
Auditor-General (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 (56 of

lakh fifty thousand rupees per mensem by the High Court and Supreme Court 
Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Act, 2018 (10 of 2018), s. 6 
(w.e.f. 1-1-2016).

nodes.title: Tribes Advisory Council
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions related to the governance and administration of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in India as per the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Tribes Advisory Council**: The document specifies the composition and responsibilities of the Tribes Advisory Council, which advises the Governor on matters concerning the welfare and advancement of Scheduled Tribes. It details the appointment of council members and the conduct of its meetings.

2. **Governor's Powers**: The Governor has the authority to regulate the application of laws in Scheduled Areas, including the ability to exempt certain Acts from applying to these areas or to modify their application. The Governor can also make regulations for the governance of Scheduled Areas, including land transfer restrictions and business regulations for money-lenders.

3. **Scheduled Areas Definition**: The document defines "Scheduled Areas" and outlines the President's authority to declare or modify these areas, including the ability to increase or alter boundaries after consulting with the Governor.

4. **Regulatory Framework**: Regulations made by the Governor must be submitted to the President for assent, and consultation with the Tribes Advisory Council is required before making such regulations.

Overall, the document emphasizes the special provisions and governance mechanisms established for the protection and advancement of Scheduled Tribes and their territories in India.

nodes.title: Constitution of District Councils and Regional Councils
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions related to the governance of autonomous districts and regions in India as specified in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Governor's Authority**: The Governor can issue orders regarding the administration of autonomous districts after considering reports from a designated Commission.

2. **District and Regional Councils**: Each autonomous district will have a District Council with a maximum of thirty members, including elected representatives and those nominated by the Governor. Additionally, separate Regional Councils will be established for autonomous regions.

3. **Council Composition and Elections**: The document details the composition, election procedures, and qualifications for members of the District and Regional Councils, emphasizing adult suffrage and the role of the Governor in rule-making.

4. **Powers and Administration**: The District and Regional Councils are granted specific powers for local governance, including the ability to make laws on various subjects such as education, agriculture, and infrastructure, subject to the Governor's assent.

5. **Amendments and Provisions**: The text references amendments to the provisions applicable to specific states, particularly Assam, highlighting changes in council names and member composition.

6. **Term and Conduct of Business**: It specifies the term of office for elected members and the procedures for conducting business within the councils, including the formation of subordinate local councils.

Overall, the document emphasizes the framework for self-governance in tribal areas, ensuring representation and administrative autonomy while maintaining oversight by the Governor.

nodes.title: Powers of the District Councils and Regional Councils to make laws
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions related to the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India, which pertains to the governance and administration of autonomous regions and districts, particularly in the northeastern states. Key points include:

1. **Elections and Governance**: It discusses the rules for elections to the councils and the powers of the District and Regional Councils to make laws, emphasizing the role of the Governor in approving these laws.

2. **Law-Making Powers**: The document details the specific areas in which the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council, Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, and Bodoland Territorial Council can legislate, covering topics such as agriculture, education, health, and local governance.

3. **Administration of Justice**: It describes the establishment of village councils or courts for resolving disputes among Scheduled Tribes, outlining their jurisdiction and the appeal process to higher courts.

4. **Financial Management**: Provisions for the creation of District and Regional Funds for managing finances related to the councils' administration are included, along with the powers to assess land revenue and impose taxes.

5. **Regulation of Trade and Money-Lending**: The document grants District Councils the authority to regulate money-lending and trading activities by non-tribals, ensuring the protection of local interests.

6. **Publication of Laws**: It mandates that all laws, rules, and regulations made by the councils must be published in the Official Gazette to have legal effect.

7. **Application of State and Central Laws**: The document specifies how Acts of Parliament and state legislation apply to autonomous districts and regions, with amendments noted for specific councils.

Overall, the document emphasizes the autonomy and legislative powers of local councils in managing their affairs while ensuring oversight by the state and central authorities.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the provisions related to the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram as specified in the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. It discusses the establishment of autonomous districts and regions within these tribal areas, detailing the Governor's authority to create, modify, or redefine these districts and regions. Key points include the ability to divide areas inhabited by different Scheduled Tribes into autonomous regions, include or exclude areas from designated parts of the schedule, create new autonomous districts, and alter the boundaries or names of existing districts. The document also notes amendments and provisions specific to certain areas, such as the Bodoland Territorial Areas District.

PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the procedure and power of the Parliament to amend the Constitution of India as specified in Article 368. It states that Parliament can amend the Constitution through a Bill introduced in either House, requiring a majority of total membership and a two-thirds majority of those present and voting. Certain amendments, particularly those affecting specific articles and provisions, must also be ratified by at least half of the state legislatures. Additionally, it clarifies that amendments made under this article are not subject to judicial review and asserts that there are no limitations on Parliament's constituent power to amend the Constitution.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines key provisions related to elections in India as specified in Part XV of the Constitution. It discusses the roles and responsibilities of the Election Commission, including the appointment and removal of Election Commissioners, and the requirement for the President or State Governors to provide necessary staff to the Election Commission. It establishes that no individual can be excluded from electoral rolls based on religion, race, caste, or sex, ensuring inclusivity in the electoral process. The document also states that elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies are based on adult suffrage, allowing all citizens aged eighteen and above to register as voters, barring certain disqualifications. Additionally, it grants Parliament the authority to legislate on various electoral matters, including the preparation of electoral rolls and delimitation of constituencies.

Commission or to a Regional Commissioner such staff as may be necessary for

325. No person to be ineligible for inclusion in, or to claim to be 
included in a special, electoral roll on grounds of religion, race, caste or 
sex.—There shall be one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency 
for election to either House of Parliament or to the House or either House of the 
Legislature of a State and no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in any such 
roll or claim to be included in any special electoral roll for any such 
constituency on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them.
326. Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative 
Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage.—The elections to 
the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be 
on the basis of adult suffrage; that is to say, every person who is a citizen of 
India and who is not less than 2[eighteen years] of age on such date as may be 
fixed in that behalf by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature 
and is not otherwise disqualified under this Constitution or any law made by 
the appropriate Legislature on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of 
mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a 
voter at any such election.  
327. Power of Parliament to make provision with respect to elections 
to Legislatures.—Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, Parliament 
may from time to time by law make provision with respect to all matters 
relating to, or in connection with, elections to either House of Parliament or to 
the House or either House of the Legislature of a State including the 
preparation of electoral rolls, the delimitation of constituencies and all other 
matters necessary for securing  the due constitution of such House or Houses.

nodes.summary:
The partial document discusses provisions related to the administration of autonomous districts and regions in the State of Mizoram as outlined in the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. Key points include:

1. The President's authority to exempt certain Acts of Parliament from applying to autonomous districts or regions, with the possibility of retrospective effect.
2. The requirement for estimated receipts and expenditures of autonomous districts to be presented separately in the annual financial statement after discussion with the District Council.
3. The Governor's power to appoint a Commission to investigate and report on various aspects of administration in autonomous districts, including educational and medical facilities, the need for new legislation, and the administration of local laws.
4. The process for laying the Commission's report before the State Legislature, along with the government's proposed actions.
5. The Governor's ability to annul or suspend acts and resolutions of District and Regional Councils if they threaten national safety or public order, including the procedure for legislative oversight of such actions.

body considered suitable by him for a period not exceeding twelve 
months:
Provided that when an order under clause (a) of this paragraph has 
been made, the Governor may take the action referred to in clause (b) of this 
paragraph with regard to the administration of the area in question pending 
the reconstitution of the Council on fresh general election:
Provided further that no action shall be taken under clause (b) of this 
paragraph without giving the District or the Regional Council, as the case 
may be, an opportunity of placing its views before the Legislature of the 
State.
