(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
248
373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
249
375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and 
pension as are provided for under clause (3) of article 148 in respect of the 
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and be entitled to continue to hold office 
until the expiration of his term of office as determined under the provisions which 
were applicable to him immediately before such commencement.
______________________________________________

316 but subject to the proviso to clause (2) of that article, continue to hold office 
until the expiration of their term of office as determined under the rules which  were 
applicable immediately before such commencement to such members.

392. Power of the President to remove difficulties.—(1) The President 
may, for the purpose of removing any difficulties, particularly in relation to the 
transition from the provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935, to the 
provisions of this Constitution, by order direct that this Constitution shall, 
during such period as may be specified in the order, have effect subject to such 
adaptations, whether by way of modification, addition or omission, as he may 
deem to be necessary or expedient:
Provided that no such order shall be made after the first meeting of 
Parliament duly constituted under Chapter II of Part V.
(2) Every order made under clause (1) shall be laid before Parliament.
(3) The powers conferred on the President by this article, by article 324, by 
clause (3) of article 367 and by article 391 shall, before the commencement of this 
Constitution, be exercisable by the Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

252
PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines temporary and transitional provisions in the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the powers of Parliament regarding certain matters in the State List and special provisions related to the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It grants Parliament the authority to legislate on specific subjects as if they were in the Concurrent List for a period of five years from the Constitution's commencement. These subjects include trade, commerce, and various commodities such as textiles, foodstuffs, and minerals. Additionally, it details the limitations on Parliament's power to legislate for Jammu and Kashmir, emphasizing the need for consultation with the State Government and the President's declaration regarding the applicability of laws. The document also references the modification of Article 370, which previously granted special autonomy to Jammu and Kashmir, indicating that most provisions of the Constitution now apply to the state without exceptions.

PART XXI
1[TEMPORARY, TRANSITIONAL AND 
SPECIAL PROVISIONS] 
369. Temporary power to Parliament to make laws with respect to 
certain matters in the State List as if they were matters in the Concurrent 
List.—Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, Parliament shall, during 
a period of five years from the commencement of this Constitution, have power 
to make laws with respect to the following matters as if they were enumerated 
in the Concurrent List, namely:— 
(a) trade and commerce within a State in, and the production, supply 
and distribution of, cotton and woollen textiles, raw cotton (including 
ginned cotton and unginned cotton or kapas), cotton seed, paper 
(including newsprint), food-stuffs (including edible oilseeds and oil), 
cattle fodder (including oil-cakes and other concentrates), coal 
(including coke and derivatives of coal), iron, steel and mica;
(b) offences against laws with respect to any of the matters mentioned
in clause (a), jurisdiction and powers of all courts except the Supreme 
Court with respect to any of those matters, and fees in respect of any of 
those matters but not including fees taken in any court,
but any law made by Parliament, which Parliament would not but for the 
provisions of this article have been competent to make, shall, to the extent of the 
incompetency, cease to have effect on the expiration of the said period, except as 
respects things done or omitted to be done before the expiration thereof.

AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS" (w.e.f. 1-12-1963).

374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The

jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory

any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.

the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the

India.

nodes.title: 394. Commencement.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines specific provisions of the Constitution of India related to temporary, transitional, and special arrangements for various states, particularly focusing on Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka. Key points include:

1. **Legal Validity of Appointments**: Provisions ensuring that certain appointments and transfers are not deemed illegal based on residency requirements in specific states.
2. **Establishment of Universities**: The authority of Parliament to establish a Central University in Andhra Pradesh.
3. **Special Provisions for Sikkim**: Details regarding the composition and functioning of the Legislative Assembly, representation in the House of the People, and the Governor's responsibilities for social and economic advancement.
4. **Mizoram's Autonomy**: Restrictions on the applicability of Parliament's acts concerning Mizo customs and laws unless decided by the state assembly.
5. **Arunachal Pradesh's Governance**: The Governor's special responsibility for law and order, with provisions for individual judgment in decision-making.
6. **Karnataka's Development Board**: Special responsibilities for the Governor regarding the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, including equitable development and employment opportunities.
7. **Continuance of Existing Laws**: Provisions for the continuation and adaptation of existing laws until amended or repealed by competent authorities.
8. **Judicial Provisions**: Transition of judges and ongoing legal proceedings from the Federal Court to the Supreme Court, along with the continuation of judicial functions across various jurisdictions.
9. **Presidential Powers**: The President's authority to adapt laws and remove difficulties during the transition to the new constitutional framework.

Overall, the document emphasizes the unique legal and administrative frameworks established for specific states within India, ensuring their governance aligns with the broader constitutional provisions.

393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

Provided that if any question arises whether any matter is or is not a 
matter as respects which the Governor is under this clause required to act 
in the exercise of his individual judgment, the decision of the Governor in 
his discretion shall be final, and the validity of anything done by the 
Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or 
ought not to have acted in the exercise of his individual judgment:
Provided further that if the President on receipt of a report from 
the Governor or otherwise is satisfied that it is no longer necessary for 
the Governor to have special responsibility with respect to law and order 
in the State of Arunachal Pradesh, he may by order direct that the 
Governor shall cease to have such responsibility with effect from such

2[371J. Special provisions with respect to State of Karnataka.—
(1) The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Karnataka, 
provide for any special responsibility of the Governor for—
(a) establishment of a separate development board for Hyderabad-
Karnataka region with the provision that a report on the working of the 
board will be placed each year before the State Legislative Assembly; 
(b) equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure 
over the said region, subject  to the requirements of the State as a whole; 
and 
(c) equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging 
to the said region, in matters of public employment, education and 
vocational training, subject to the requirements of the State as a whole.
(2) An order made under sub- clause (c) of clause (1) may provide for—
(a) reservation of a proportion of  seats educational and vocational 
training institutions in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region for students who 
belong to that region by birth or by domicile; and

(b) identification of posts or classes of posts under the State

372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.—(1) 
Notwithstanding the repeal by this Constitution of the enactments referred to in 
article 395 but subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, all the law in 
force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended 
by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
(2) For the purpose of bringing the provisions of any law in force in the 
territory of India into accord with the provisions of this Constitution, the 
President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, 
whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and 
provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, 
have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(3) Nothing in clause (2) shall be deemed—
(a) to empower the President to make any adaptation or 
modification of any law after the expiration of 1[three years] from the 
commencement of this Constitution; or
(b) to prevent any competent Legislature or other competent 
authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by 
the President under the said clause.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
247
Explanation I.—The expression “law in force” in this article shall 
include a law passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in 
the territory of India before the commencement of this Constitution and not 
previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in 
operation either at all or in particular areas.
Explanation II.—Any law passed or made by a Legislature or other 
competent authority in the territory of India which immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution had extra-territorial effect as well as effect 
in the territory of India shall, subject to any such adaptations and modifications 
as aforesaid, continue to have such extra-territorial effect.
Explanation III.—Nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing 
any temporary law in force beyond the date fixed for its expiration or the date 
on which it would have expired if this Constitution had  not come into force.
Explanation IV.—An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a 
Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and in force 
immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless 
withdrawn by the Governor of the corresponding State earlier, cease to operate 
at the expiration of six weeks from the first meeting after such commencement 
of the Legislative Assembly of that State functioning under clause (1) of article 
382, and  nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing any such 
Ordinance in force beyond the said period.
1[372A.  Power of the President to adapt laws.—(1) For the purposes 
of bringing the provisions of any law in force in India or in any part thereof, 
immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh 
Amendment) Act, 1956, into accord with the provisions of this Constitution as 
amended by that Act, the President may by order made before the first day of 
November, 1957, make such adaptations and modifications of the law, whether 
by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and provide 
that the law shall, as from such date as may be  specified in the order, have 
effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(2) Nothing in clause (1) shall be deemed to  prevent a competent 
Legislature or other competent authority from repealing or amending any law 
adapted or modified by the President  under the said clause.]
______________________________________________
1. Ins. by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 23 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).
 See the Adaptation of Laws Order of 1956 and 1957. 

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
248
373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
249
375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and

nodes.title: Haryana
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines specific provisions of the Constitution of India related to temporary, transitional, and special arrangements for various states. Key points include:

1. **Governor's Discretion**: The Governor's decisions regarding individual judgment in certain matters are final, particularly concerning law and order in Arunachal Pradesh.

2. **Legislative Assembly Composition**: Special provisions for the composition of the Legislative Assemblies in Arunachal Pradesh and Goa, mandating a minimum number of members.

3. **Special Responsibilities in Karnataka**: The President can assign special responsibilities to the Governor of Karnataka, including the establishment of a development board for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region and ensuring equitable allocation of resources and opportunities for its residents.

4. **Continuance of Existing Laws**: Existing laws prior to the Constitution's commencement remain in force until amended or repealed, with provisions for the President to adapt these laws to align with the new Constitution.

5. **Judicial Provisions**: Judges of the Federal Court automatically become Judges of the Supreme Court, and all pending cases in the Federal Court are transferred to the Supreme Court.

6. **Public Service Commissions**: Members of existing Public Service Commissions transition to their respective roles under the new Constitution, maintaining their terms.

7. **Special Provisions for Andhra Pradesh**: The duration of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is specified to last five years unless dissolved sooner.

8. **Repeals and Commencement**: The document includes provisions for the repeal of previous acts and outlines the commencement of the Constitution, along with the establishment of an authoritative Hindi text.

Overall, the document emphasizes the transition from previous governance structures to the new constitutional framework, ensuring continuity and special provisions for certain states.

THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
245
Provided that if any question arises whether any matter is or is not a 
matter as respects which the Governor is under this clause required to act 
in the exercise of his individual judgment, the decision of the Governor in 
his discretion shall be final, and the validity of anything done by the 
Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or 
ought not to have acted in the exercise of his individual judgment:
Provided further that if the President on receipt of a report from 
the Governor or otherwise is satisfied that it is no longer necessary for 
the Governor to have special responsibility with respect to law and order 
in the State of Arunachal Pradesh, he may by order direct that the 
Governor shall cease to have such responsibility with effect from such 
date as may be specified in the order;
(b) the Legislative Assembly of the State of Arunachal Pradesh 
shall consist of not less than thirty members.]
1[371-I. Special provision with respect to the State of Goa.—
Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution, the Legislative Assembly of the 
State of Goa shall consist of not less than thirty members.]
2[371J. Special provisions with respect to State of Karnataka.—
(1) The President may, by order made with respect to the State of Karnataka, 
provide for any special responsibility of the Governor for—
(a) establishment of a separate development board for Hyderabad-
Karnataka region with the provision that a report on the working of the 
board will be placed each year before the State Legislative Assembly; 
(b) equitable allocation of funds for developmental expenditure 
over the said region, subject  to the requirements of the State as a whole; 
and 
(c) equitable opportunities and facilities for the people belonging 
to the said region, in matters of public employment, education and 
vocational training, subject to the requirements of the State as a whole.
(2) An order made under sub- clause (c) of clause (1) may provide for—
(a) reservation of a proportion of  seats educational and vocational 
training institutions in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region for students who 
belong to that region by birth or by domicile; and

(b) identification of posts or classes of posts under the State 
Government and in any body or organisation under the control of the 
State Government in the Hyderabad-Karnataka region and reservation of 
a proportion of such posts for persons who belong to that region by birth 
or by domicile and for appointment thereto by direct recruitment or by 
promotion or in any other manner as may be specified in the order.]
372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.—(1) 
Notwithstanding the repeal by this Constitution of the enactments referred to in 
article 395 but subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, all the law in 
force in the territory of India immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall continue in force therein until altered or repealed or amended 
by a competent Legislature or other competent authority.
(2) For the purpose of bringing the provisions of any law in force in the 
territory of India into accord with the provisions of this Constitution, the 
President may by order make such adaptations and modifications of such law, 
whether by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and 
provide that the law shall, as from such date as may be specified in the order, 
have effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(3) Nothing in clause (2) shall be deemed—
(a) to empower the President to make any adaptation or 
modification of any law after the expiration of 1[three years] from the 
commencement of this Constitution; or
(b) to prevent any competent Legislature or other competent 
authority from repealing or amending any law adapted or modified by 
the President under the said clause.

Explanation I.—The expression “law in force” in this article shall 
include a law passed or made by a Legislature or other competent authority in 
the territory of India before the commencement of this Constitution and not 
previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in 
operation either at all or in particular areas.
Explanation II.—Any law passed or made by a Legislature or other 
competent authority in the territory of India which immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution had extra-territorial effect as well as effect 
in the territory of India shall, subject to any such adaptations and modifications 
as aforesaid, continue to have such extra-territorial effect.
Explanation III.—Nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing 
any temporary law in force beyond the date fixed for its expiration or the date 
on which it would have expired if this Constitution had  not come into force.
Explanation IV.—An Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of a 
Province under section 88 of the Government of India Act, 1935, and in force 
immediately before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless 
withdrawn by the Governor of the corresponding State earlier, cease to operate 
at the expiration of six weeks from the first meeting after such commencement 
of the Legislative Assembly of that State functioning under clause (1) of article 
382, and  nothing in this article shall be construed as continuing any such 
Ordinance in force beyond the said period.
1[372A.  Power of the President to adapt laws.—(1) For the purposes 
of bringing the provisions of any law in force in India or in any part thereof, 
immediately before the commencement of the Constitution (Seventh 
Amendment) Act, 1956, into accord with the provisions of this Constitution as 
amended by that Act, the President may by order made before the first day of 
November, 1957, make such adaptations and modifications of the law, whether 
by way of repeal or amendment, as may be necessary or expedient, and provide 
that the law shall, as from such date as may be  specified in the order, have 
effect subject to the adaptations and modifications so made, and any such 
adaptation or modification shall not be questioned in any court of law.
(2) Nothing in clause (1) shall be deemed to  prevent a competent 
Legislature or other competent authority from repealing or amending any law 
adapted or modified by the President  under the said clause.]

373. Power of President to make order in respect of persons under 
preventive detention in certain cases.—Until provision is made by Parliament 
under clause (7) of article 22, or until the expiration of one year from the 
commencement of this Constitution, whichever  is earlier, the said  article shall 
have effect as if for any reference to Parliament in clauses (4) and (7) thereof 
there were substituted a reference to the President and for any reference to any 
law made by Parliament in those clauses there were substituted a reference to 
an order made by the President.
374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

375. Courts, authorities and officers to continue to function subject 
to the provisions of the Constitution.—All courts of civil, criminal and 
revenue jurisdiction, all authorities and all officers, judicial, executive and 
ministerial, throughout the territory of India, shall continue to exercise their 
respective functions subject to the provisions of this Constitution.
376. Provisions as to Judges of High Courts.—(1) Notwithstanding 
anything in clause (2) of article 217, the Judges of a High Court in any 
Province holding office immediately before the commencement of this 
Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Judges of the High Court in the corresponding State, and 
shall thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in  
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 221 in 
respect of the Judges of such High Court. 1[Any such Judge shall, 
notwithstanding that he is not a citizen of India, be eligible for appointment as 
Chief Justice of such High Court, or as Chief Justice or other Judge of any 
other High Court.] 
(2) The Judges of a High Court in any Indian State corresponding to any 
State specified in Part B of the First Schedule holding office immediately 
before the commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected 
otherwise, become on such commencement the Judges of the High Court in the 
State so specified and shall, notwithstanding anything in clauses  (1) and (2) of 
article 217 but subject to the proviso to clause (1) of that article, continue to hold 
office until the expiration of such period as the President may by order determine. 
(3)  In this article, the expression “Judge” does not include an acting Judge 
or an additional Judge.
377. Provisions as to Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.—The 
Auditor-General of India holding office immediately before the commencement of 
this Constitution shall, unless  he has elected otherwise, become on such 
commencement the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and shall thereupon 
be entitled to such salaries and to such rights in respect of leave of absence and 
pension as are provided for under clause (3) of article 148 in respect of the 
Comptroller and Auditor-General of India and be entitled to continue to hold office 
until the expiration of his term of office as determined under the provisions which 
were applicable to him immediately before such commencement.

PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

nodes.title: SECOND SCHEDULE
PART A PROVISIONS AS TO THE PRESIDENT AND THE GOVERNORS OF STATES
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines provisions related to the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of the President of India and the Governors of States, as well as the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People and the Council of States, and their counterparts in State Legislatures. It specifies the monthly salaries for the President (10,000 rupees) and Governors (5,500 rupees), along with allowances equivalent to those previously held by the Governor-General and provincial governors before the Constitution's commencement. It also states that individuals acting in these roles are entitled to the same benefits. Additionally, it details the salaries and allowances for the legislative leaders, ensuring they align with those of their predecessors in the Dominion of India. The document includes references to amendments and changes made to the original provisions.

nodes.title: PART C PROVISIONS AS TO THE SPEAKER AND THE DEPUTY SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE OF THE PEOPLE AND THE CHAIRMAN AND THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN OF THE COUNCIL OF STATES
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines provisions related to the salaries and allowances of key legislative and judicial positions in India as specified in the Constitution. It details the compensation for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the House of the People, the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, as well as the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council of a State. The document specifies that these salaries are to be based on the amounts that were in effect prior to the Constitution's commencement. Additionally, it includes provisions for the salaries of Judges of the Supreme Court, detailing specific salary rates for the Chief Justice and other Judges, along with conditions regarding pension adjustments and the provision of official residences for Judges. The text also notes amendments made to these provisions over time.

nodes.title: PART D PROVISIONS AS TO THE JUDGES OF THE SUPREME COURT AND OF THE HIGH COURTS
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines provisions related to the salaries, allowances, and conditions of service for the Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts in India, as specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution. It details the monthly salary rates for the Chief Justice and other judges, stipulating reductions in salary for those receiving pensions from previous government service. It also mentions the entitlement of judges to official residences without rent, travel allowances, and the governance of their leave and pension rights based on prior provisions applicable to the Federal Court judges. Additionally, it includes similar provisions for the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, highlighting their salary and conditions of service. The document reflects amendments made over time, including significant salary increases.

nodes.title: PART E PROVISIONS AS TO THE COMPTROLLER AND AUDITOR-GENERAL OF INDIA
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines specific provisions from the Constitution of India, focusing on the roles and responsibilities of judges and the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India. It defines terms related to judicial service, including the inclusion of acting and ad hoc judges, and details what constitutes "actual service" for judges. Additionally, it specifies the salary and conditions of service for the Comptroller and Auditor-General, including provisions for special pay for those transitioning from the role of Auditor-General. The document also includes forms of oaths for various government officials, such as ministers and candidates for election to Parliament, emphasizing their commitment to uphold the Constitution and maintain confidentiality in their duties.

11. In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires,—
(a) the expression “Chief Justice” includes an acting Chief Justice,

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the provisions related to the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of the President of India and the Governors of the States as specified in the Second Schedule of the Constitution. It states the monthly salaries for the President (10,000 rupees) and the Governors (5,500 rupees), and mentions that they are entitled to allowances similar to those received by their predecessors before the Constitution came into effect. Additionally, it affirms that the President and Governors will retain the same privileges as the former Governor-General and provincial Governors. It also specifies that individuals acting in these roles will receive the same emoluments and privileges as the officials they are replacing.

It includes the oath of office for Union Ministers, State Ministers, candidates for election to Parliament and State Legislatures, members of Parliament and State Legislatures, as well as judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts. Each oath emphasizes allegiance to the Constitution of India, the commitment to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of the nation, and the duty to perform their responsibilities without fear or favor. Additionally, the document includes a Fourth Schedule that details the allocation of seats in the Council of States for various states and Union territories, indicating the number of seats assigned to each.

nodes.title: FIFTH SCHEDULE
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the provisions related to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in India, as specified in the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution. It includes several key points:

1. **Interpretation and Scope**: Defines "State" in the context of Scheduled Areas, excluding certain northeastern states.

2. **Executive Power**: States that the executive power of a State extends to Scheduled Areas, with the Governor required to report to the President on their administration.

3. **Tribes Advisory Council**: Establishes the requirement for a Tribes Advisory Council in states with Scheduled Areas, detailing its composition, duties, and the Governor's authority to regulate its functioning.

4. **Law Applicability**: Grants the Governor the power to exempt certain laws from applying to Scheduled Areas and to make regulations for governance, including land transfer and business practices among Scheduled Tribes.

5. **Scheduled Areas Definition**: Defines Scheduled Areas and outlines the President's authority to declare, modify, or rescind such areas.

6. **Amendment of the Schedule**: Allows Parliament to amend the provisions of the Schedule without it being considered a constitutional amendment.

Overall, the document emphasizes the governance framework for Scheduled Areas and the rights and protections for Scheduled Tribes within those regions.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines provisions related to the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India, specifically focusing on the powers and responsibilities of the North Cachar Hills Autonomous Council and the Bodoland Territorial Council. It details various subjects over which these councils have legislative authority, including water management, social security, public health, agriculture, education, and cultural affairs. The document also describes the process for submitting laws made by these councils to the Governor for consideration by the President, including the possibility of the President returning laws for reconsideration. Additionally, it emphasizes the protection of existing land rights for citizens and the conditions under which land acquisition can occur within the Bodoland Territorial Areas District.

nodes.title: Administration of justice in autonomous districts and autonomous regions.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions related to the administration of justice in autonomous districts and regions as specified in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India. Key points include:

1. **Law Submission and Effect**: Laws made under the specified provisions must be submitted to the Governor for assent before taking effect.

2. **Village Councils and Courts**: Regional and District Councils can establish village councils or courts to handle disputes among Scheduled Tribes, excluding certain cases. They have the authority to appoint members and presiding officers for these councils and courts.

3. **Court Jurisdiction**: The Regional or District Councils have appellate jurisdiction over cases tried by village councils, with the High Court and Supreme Court retaining jurisdiction over specified matters.

4. **Rule-Making Authority**: Councils can create rules regarding the constitution and powers of village councils and courts, trial procedures, and enforcement of decisions, subject to the Governor's approval.

5. **Governor's Powers**: The Governor can confer powers under the Code of Civil Procedure and the Code of Criminal Procedure to District and Regional Councils for specific cases and may withdraw or modify these powers.

6. **Establishment of Local Institutions**: District Councils can establish and manage primary schools, dispensaries, and other local institutions, with regulations subject to the Governor's approval.

7. **Financial Provisions**: Each autonomous district and region will have designated funds to manage financial resources received by the respective councils for administration.

Overall, the document emphasizes the autonomy of local councils in governance and justice administration while outlining the oversight role of the Governor.

The partial document outlines provisions related to the governance and administrative powers of autonomous districts and regions in India as specified in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Governor's Authority**: The document specifies that the Governor cannot confer certain powers to District or Regional Councils in autonomous areas without presidential appointment.

2. **District Council Powers**: It details the powers of District Councils to establish and manage primary schools, dispensaries, markets, and other local infrastructure, with the Governor's prior approval for regulations.

3. **District and Regional Funds**: It establishes the creation of District and Regional Funds for financial management, including rules for their management, auditing by the Comptroller and Auditor-General, and procedures for handling funds.

4. **Taxation Powers**: The document grants District and Regional Councils the authority to assess and collect land revenue, impose taxes on lands and buildings, and levy various local taxes, including those on professions and vehicles. 

Overall, the document emphasizes the autonomy and administrative responsibilities of local councils in managing resources and governance within their respective regions.

nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions from the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution of India, focusing on the governance and financial management of autonomous districts and regions. Key points include:

1. The Governor's authority to establish rules for managing District and Regional Funds, including procedures for financial transactions and auditing by the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
2. The powers of Regional and District Councils to assess and collect land revenue and impose various taxes, such as on professions, trades, and property, as well as tolls on residents.
3. Regulations that District Councils can create to control money-lending and trading activities by non-tribals, including licensing requirements and interest rate limits.
4. Provisions for the distribution of royalties from mineral extraction to District Councils, with mechanisms for resolving disputes regarding these royalties.

Overall, the document emphasizes the financial autonomy and regulatory powers granted to local councils in managing resources and economic activities within their jurisdictions.

Additionally, it states that all laws and regulations made under this Schedule must be published in the Official Gazette to have legal force.

nodes.title: Application of Acts of Parliament and of the Legislature of the State of Tripura to the autonomous districts and autonomous regions in the State of Tripura.
nodes.summary:
The partial document discusses provisions related to the governance and administration of autonomous districts and regions in the states of Tripura and Mizoram as outlined in the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Legislative Applicability**: The document specifies how acts of the state legislature and Parliament can be applied or exempted in autonomous districts and regions, with provisions for the Governor and President to issue notifications regarding their applicability, including potential retrospective effects.

2. **District Council Authority**: It emphasizes the role of District Councils in directing the application of state laws, particularly concerning matters like the consumption of non-distilled alcoholic liquor, and allows them to modify the application of such laws.

3. **Financial Management**: It mandates that estimated receipts and expenditures related to autonomous districts be presented separately in the state's annual financial statement, ensuring transparency and accountability.

4. **Commission for Administration Review**: The Governor has the authority to appoint a Commission to investigate and report on various aspects of administration in autonomous districts, including educational and medical facilities, the need for new legislation, and the enforcement of laws by District and Regional Councils. 

Overall, the document outlines the framework for legislative and administrative autonomy in specific regions, ensuring local governance while maintaining oversight from state and national authorities.

nodes.summary:
The partial document discusses provisions related to the administration of autonomous districts in India as outlined in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. Key points include:

1. The Governor's authority to assume functions of the District or Regional Council if the administration cannot be conducted as per the Schedule, with the possibility of extending this authority for up to six months.
2. The requirement for any order made by the Governor to be presented to the State Legislature, which must approve it within thirty days for it to remain in effect.
3. The Governor's power to exclude certain areas from autonomous districts for the purpose of forming constituencies for elections to the Legislative Assemblies of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, or Mizoram.
4. Transitional provisions for the establishment of District Councils, stating that until such councils are formed, the Governor will administer the districts, including the ability to modify or repeal existing laws applicable to those areas.
5. The provision for the formation of an Interim Executive Council for the Bodoland Territorial Areas District in Assam, aimed at including representation from both tribal and non-tribal communities, with a six-month duration to facilitate elections.

119. Transitional provisions.—(1) As soon as possible after the

effect.

nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines provisions related to the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram, as specified in the Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. Key points include:

1. **Autonomous Districts and Regions**: It establishes that tribal areas are designated as autonomous districts, with the Governor having the authority to create autonomous regions within these districts based on the presence of different Scheduled Tribes.

2. **Governor's Powers**: The Governor can modify the boundaries of autonomous districts, create new districts, and make other administrative changes, subject to certain conditions and the consideration of reports from appointed commissions.

3. **District and Regional Councils**: Each autonomous district will have a District Council, consisting of elected and nominated members, while autonomous regions will have separate Regional Councils. The councils are responsible for local governance and administration.

4. **Elections and Composition**: The document details the composition, election process, and powers of the District and Regional Councils, including the Governor's role in establishing rules for their functioning.

5. **Legislative Powers**: It grants District and Regional Councils the authority to make laws on various subjects, including education, agriculture, public health, and local governance, with certain laws requiring the Governor's assent before taking effect.

6. **Amendments and Provisions**: The document includes references to amendments made to the provisions, particularly concerning the Bodoland Territorial Council and other specific councils, highlighting the evolving nature of governance in these regions. 

Overall, the document emphasizes the autonomy and self-governance of tribal areas while outlining the framework for their administration and legislative powers.

nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the procedure for amending the Constitution as specified in Article 368. It states that Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution through a Bill introduced in either House, which must be passed by a majority of the total membership and a two-thirds majority of those present and voting. The amendment must then receive the President's assent to take effect. Additionally, it specifies certain articles and provisions that require special consideration if amendments are proposed, indicating that changes to these areas involve more stringent requirements.

374. Provisions as to Judges of the Federal Court and proceedings 
pending in the Federal Court or before His Majesty in Council.—(1) The 
Judges of the Federal Court holding office immediately before the 
commencement of this Constitution shall, unless they have elected otherwise, 
become on such commencement the Judges of the Supreme Court and shall 
thereupon be entitled to such salaries and allowances and to such rights in 
respect of leave of absence and pension as are provided for under article 125 in 
respect of the Judges of the Supreme Court.
(2) All suits, appeals and proceedings, civil or criminal, pending in the 
Federal Court at the commencement of this Constitution shall stand removed to 
the Supreme Court, and the Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to hear and 
determine the same, and the judgments and  orders of the Federal Court delivered 
or made before the  commencement of this Constitution shall have the same force 
and effect as if they had been delivered or made by the Supreme Court.
(3) Nothing in this Constitution shall operate to invalidate the exercise of 
jurisdiction by His Majesty in Council to dispose of appeals and petitions from, 
or in respect of, any judgment, decree or order of any court within the territory 
of India in so far as the exercise of such jurisdiction is authorised by law, and 
any order of His Majesty in Council made on any such appeal or petition after 
the commencement of this Constitution shall for all purposes have effect as if it 
were an order or decree made by the Supreme Court in the exercise of the  
jurisdiction conferred on such Court by this Constitution.
(4) On and from the commencement of this Constitution the jurisdiction of 
the authority functioning as the Privy Council in a State specified in Part B of the 
First Schedule to entertain and dispose of appeals and petitions from or in respect 
of any judgment, decree or order of any court within that State shall cease, and all 
appeals and other proceedings pending before the said authority at such 
commencement shall be transferred to, and disposed of by, the Supreme Court.
(5) Further provision may be made by Parliament by law to give effect to 
the provisions of this article.

PART XXII
SHORT TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, 1[AUTHORITATIVE 
TEXT IN HINDI] AND REPEALS
393. Short title.—This Constitution may be called the Constitution of 
India. 
394.  Commencement.—This article and articles 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 60,  324, 
366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393 shall come into force at once, and 
the remaining provisions of this Constitution shall come into force on the 
twenty-sixth day of January, 1950, which day is referred to in this Constitution 
as the commencement of this Constitution. 
2[394A. Authoritative text in the Hindi language.—(1) The President 
shall cause to be published under his authority,— 
(a) the translation of this Constitution in the Hindi language, 
signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, with such 
modifications as may be necessary to bring it in conformity with the 
language, style and terminology adopted in the authoritative texts of 
Central Acts in the Hindi language, and incorporating therein all the 
amendments of this Constitution made before such publication; and
(b) the translation in the Hindi language of every amendment of 
this Constitution made in the English language. 
(2) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under clause (1) shall be construed to have the same meaning as  the 
original thereof and if any difficulty arises in so construing any part of such 
translation, the President shall cause the same to be revised suitably.
(3) The translation of this Constitution and of every amendment thereof 
published under this article shall  be deemed to be, for all purposes, the 
authoritative text thereof in the Hindi language.]
395. Repeals.—
The Indian Independence Act, 1947, and the 
Government of India Act, 1935, together with all enactments amending or 
supplementing the latter Act, but not including the Abolition of Privy Council 
Jurisdiction Act, 1949, are hereby repealed.

370. Temporary provisions with respect to the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
nodes.summary: The partial document discusses specific provisions of the Constitution of India related to the State of Jammu and Kashmir and other states, focusing on temporary, transitional, and special provisions. It outlines the limitations on Parliament's power to legislate for Jammu and Kashmir, emphasizing the need for consultation with the state government and the President's authority to declare certain articles operative or inoperative. The document also mentions the special provisions for the states of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Nagaland, detailing the responsibilities of the Governor and the autonomy of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly regarding specific laws. Overall, it highlights the unique constitutional status and governance arrangements for these regions within India.

(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)

1[370. Temporary provisions with respect  to the State of Jammu 
and Kashmir.—(1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,— 
(a) the provisions of article 238 shall not apply in relation to the State 
of  Jammu and Kashmir; 
(b) the power of Parliament to make laws for the said State shall be 
limited to—
(i) those matters in the Union List and  the Concurrent List 
which, in consultation with the Government of the State, are declared 
by the President to correspond to matters specified in the Instrument 
of Accession governing the accession of the State to the Dominion  of 
India as the matters with respect to which the Dominion Legislature 
may make laws for that State; and
______________________________________________
In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (3) of article 370 read with clause (1) of 
article 370 of the Constitution of India, the President, on the recommendation of 
Parliament, is pleased to declare that, as from the 6th August, 2019 all clauses of said 
article 370 shall cease to be operative except the following which shall read as under, 
namely:—
“370. All provisions of this Constitution, as amended from time to time, 
without any modifications or exceptions, shall apply to the State of Jammu and 
Kashmir notwithstanding anything contrary contained in article 152 or article 308 or 
any other article of this Constitution or any other provision of the Constitution of 
Jammu and Kashmir or any law, document, judgment, ordinance, order, by-law, rule, 
regulation, notification, custom or usage having the force of law in the territory of 
India, or any other instrument, treaty or agreement as envisaged under article 363 or 
otherwise.”.
(See Appendix III) (C.O. 273).
1. In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (3) of the Constitution of India, the 
President, on the recommendation of the Constituent Assembly of the State of Jammu 
and Kashmir, declared that, as from the 17th day of November, 1952, the said art. 370 
shall be operative with the modification that for the Explanation in cl. (1) thereof, the 
following Explanation is substituted, namely:—
“Explanation.–For the purposes of this article, the Government of the State means 
the person for the time being recognised by the President on the recommendation of 
the Legislative Assembly of the State as the *Sadar-I-Riyasat of Jammu and Kashmir, 
acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers of the State for the time being in

(C.O. 44, dated the 15th November, 1952).

It details the responsibilities of the President and Governors in these states, including the establishment of development boards, equitable allocation of funds, and provisions for technical education and employment. The document emphasizes the unique administrative and legislative frameworks established for these states to address their specific needs and circumstances.

nodes.title: 371D. Special provisions with respect to the State of Andhra Pradesh or the State of Telangana.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines specific provisions in the Constitution of India related to temporary, transitional, and special arrangements for certain states, particularly focusing on the states of Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Sikkim. Key points include:

1. **Manipur**: The President can establish a committee within the Legislative Assembly to represent the Hill Areas, with the Governor required to report on the administration of these areas.

2. **Andhra Pradesh and Telangana**: The President may create provisions for equitable opportunities in public employment and education, allowing for local recruitment and reservation based on residency. An Administrative Tribunal can be established to handle matters related to civil service appointments and grievances.

3. **Sikkim**: The Legislative Assembly must consist of at least thirty members, and the existing assembly formed in 1974 is recognized as duly constituted under the Constitution.

Overall, the document emphasizes the unique administrative needs and governance structures for these states, ensuring representation and local considerations in legislative and employment matters.

nodes.title: 371F. Special provisions with respect to the State of Sikkim.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines specific provisions related to the State of Sikkim and other northeastern states of India, as part of the Constitution of India. Key points include:

1. **Legislative Assembly**: The term of the Legislative Assembly for Sikkim is set to four years, starting from the appointed day, with provisions for one parliamentary constituency.
2. **Representation**: The representative for Sikkim in the House of the People will be elected by the members of its Legislative Assembly.
3. **Protection of Rights**: Provisions are made for ensuring representation of different population sections in the Legislative Assembly and for delimiting constituencies accordingly.
4. **Governor's Role**: The Governor of Sikkim has special responsibilities for maintaining peace and promoting social and economic advancement among various population groups.
5. **Property and Assets**: All properties and assets vested in the Government of Sikkim before the appointed day will transfer to the Government of the State of Sikkim.
6. **Judicial Continuity**: The existing High Court and other judicial authorities will continue to function post-appointment day, and all laws in force will remain until amended or repealed.
7. **Presidential Powers**: The President can adapt laws for Sikkim and extend existing laws from other states, with provisions for addressing difficulties in implementation.
8. **Special Provisions for Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh**: Specific clauses outline the autonomy of these states regarding local customs, laws, and governance, emphasizing the Governor's special responsibilities in Arunachal Pradesh.

Overall, the document emphasizes the transitional arrangements and special provisions for Sikkim and other northeastern states, ensuring their unique cultural and administrative needs are recognized within the constitutional framework.

nodes.title: 371G. Special provision with respect to the State of Mizoram.
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines specific provisions in the Constitution of India related to temporary, transitional, and special arrangements for certain states. It includes details about the validity of actions taken in Sikkim prior to the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975. It also specifies special provisions for the states of Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka. For Mizoram, it states that certain parliamentary acts do not apply unless the state assembly decides otherwise, and it mandates a minimum number of assembly members. Arunachal Pradesh's provisions grant the Governor special responsibilities regarding law and order, with the Governor's discretion being final in related matters. Goa's provision establishes a minimum assembly size, while Karnataka's provisions allow the President to assign special responsibilities to the Governor for regional development, including the establishment of a development board and equitable opportunities for local residents in education and employment.

nodes.summary: The partial document discusses Article 370 of the Constitution of India, which pertains to the special status of the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It outlines the temporary provisions that were in place regarding the state's governance and the limitations on Parliament's power to legislate for Jammu and Kashmir. The document highlights the President's authority to declare modifications to Article 370, particularly noting the significant change that occurred on August 6, 2019, when most clauses of Article 370 ceased to be operative, thereby extending the full applicability of the Indian Constitution to Jammu and Kashmir. Additionally, it references a previous modification made in 1952 regarding the definition of the state government.
nodes.text:
THE CONSTITUTION OF  INDIA
(Part XXI.—Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
231
1[370. Temporary provisions with respect  to the State of Jammu 
and Kashmir.—(1) Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution,— 
(a) the provisions of article 238 shall not apply in relation to the State 
of  Jammu and Kashmir; 
(b) the power of Parliament to make laws for the said State shall be 
limited to—
(i) those matters in the Union List and  the Concurrent List 
which, in consultation with the Government of the State, are declared 
by the President to correspond to matters specified in the Instrument 
of Accession governing the accession of the State to the Dominion  of 
India as the matters with respect to which the Dominion Legislature 
may make laws for that State; and
______________________________________________
In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (3) of article 370 read with clause (1) of 
article 370 of the Constitution of India, the President, on the recommendation of 
Parliament, is pleased to declare that, as from the 6th August, 2019 all clauses of said 
article 370 shall cease to be operative except the following which shall read as under, 
namely:—
“370. All provisions of this Constitution, as amended from time to time, 
without any modifications or exceptions, shall apply to the State of Jammu and 
Kashmir notwithstanding anything contrary contained in article 152 or article 308 or 
any other article of this Constitution or any other provision of the Constitution of 
Jammu and Kashmir or any law, document, judgment, ordinance, order, by-law, rule, 
regulation, notification, custom or usage having the force of law in the territory of 
India, or any other instrument, treaty or agreement as envisaged under article 363 or 
otherwise.”.
(See Appendix III) (C.O. 273).
1. In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (3) of the Constitution of India, the 
President, on the recommendation of the Constituent Assembly of the State of Jammu 
and Kashmir, declared that, as from the 17th day of November, 1952, the said art. 370 
shall be operative with the modification that for the Explanation in cl. (1) thereof, the 
following Explanation is substituted, namely:—
“Explanation.–For the purposes of this article, the Government of the State means 
the person for the time being recognised by the President on the recommendation of 
the Legislative Assembly of the State as the *Sadar-I-Riyasat of Jammu and Kashmir, 
acting on the advice of the Council of Ministers of the State for the time being in 
office.”.
(C.O. 44, dated the 15th November, 1952).
*Now “Governor”.

nodes.title: 372. Continuance in force of existing laws and their adaptation.
nodes.summary:
The partial document discusses specific provisions of the Indian Constitution related to temporary, transitional, and special arrangements for certain states, particularly Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh. Key points include:

1. **Andhra Pradesh**: Establishment of a Central University and provisions regarding appointments and promotions that may not comply with existing laws.

2. **Sikkim**: Details about the composition and functioning of the Legislative Assembly, the allocation of parliamentary seats, special responsibilities of the Governor, and the continuation of existing laws and judicial structures post-constitutional amendments.

3. **Mizoram**: Special provisions that exempt certain laws from applying unless the state assembly decides otherwise, particularly concerning Mizo customs and land ownership.

4. **Arunachal Pradesh**: The Governor's special responsibility for law and order, emphasizing the need for consultation with the Council of Ministers in decision-making.

Overall, the document outlines how these states have unique provisions that recognize their specific cultural, legal, and administrative needs within the framework of the Indian Constitution.
